fields.features_heading: What a Tax Season Runs On
fields.features_subheading: Tax automation sends the requests and reminders around each return. Emergent builds it from a prompt; preparers keep the judgment.
fields.feature_1:
Checklists drawn from last year's return

Each client gets a list of the forms their prior-year return used, with one upload link. The list updates as files arrive, and the preparer sees every missing form by name.
fields.feature_2:
AI reads the form type on every upload

An AI step reads each uploaded file into fields such as the form type and the tax year it covers. Any field the AI is unsure of goes to a person on your team to confirm first.
fields.feature_3:
W-9s on file before the first payment

The app requests a W-9 when a contractor is added and keeps it with that contractor's payment records, ready for Form 1099-NEC reporting. The app itself files nothing.
fields.feature_4:
Reminders by email or Slack

Pick the day a reminder goes to a client and the day a late item moves to a partner. Each reminder names the missing item and links to it, with no tax figures or account numbers.
fields.feature_5:
Connects to the tools your practice runs

The app connects to any tax or accounting tool with an API, such as QuickBooks or Xero. Client and return records sync in and out, and nobody on the team types a name twice.
fields.feature_6:
Your tax app's code, in your GitHub

Export the app's full code to your GitHub repository on paid plans. Client records stay in a database you own, and your IT lead can review exactly who is able to open them.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Places Tax Paperwork Piles Up
fields.tab_content_1:
The 1098 is the one form still out

Hollisbrook Tax Group builds each client's checklist from last year's return. Marisol Penrice's list has a W-2, two 1099-INT forms, and a Form 1098. The app reads the form type and tax year on each upload and checks off 3 of the 4. With the 1098 still missing after 7 days, she gets an email reminder with her upload link.
fields.tab_content_2:
No W-9 on file, no place in the payment run

Ottaway Joinery pays 12 contractors, and 11 have a W-9 on file. When drafter Ysolde Rautio is added, the app emails her a W-9 request. Her $650.00 invoice stays out of Friday's payment run until the form arrives, and the W-9 is kept with her payment records.
fields.tab_content_3:
79 of 86 letters signed, 7 with the partner

Every engagement letter at Soderqvist Tax Partners goes out for e-signature, 86 in all. A client's prep task opens only once the letter is signed, and 79 are open. The 7 letters still unsigned after 10 days reach partner Halvard Nyquist in one Slack direct message with the client names.
fields.tab_content_4:
The board shows 9 returns short of documents

Tollgate Row Tax tracks 140 returns on one board: 52 ready to file, 18 in review, 61 in prep, and 9 waiting on documents. Each card shows the preparer and the date of the last upload. Partner Faustina Strachan gets the 9 waiting returns as one list in the app, 21 days before the firm's March 31 cutoff.

fields.howto_description: Seven steps to build tax automation for your firm's paperwork, tested on last season's clients before the next season opens.
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Start from last year's client list
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Pick the reminder and escalation days
fields.howto_step_1_des: Write down the tax work that comes back every season: document requests, W-9s, engagement letters, and status updates for partners. Next to each job, note who chases it today, which tool holds the file, and how many hours it takes.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Export last season's client list with the forms each return used. That list becomes every client's checklist, and nobody starts from a blank request. Describe the list and its rules in a prompt, and Emergent builds the tracker and its database.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Decide two numbers for each job: the day a client gets a reminder, and how many days late an item can run before a partner hears about it. Keep each reminder to the item and a link, with no tax figures in the message.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Connect your tax software and document storage through their APIs. Client names and return status then sync in both directions, and a preparer works from one record instead of retyping details from two or three tools.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Have your accountant review the rules
fields.howto_step_5_des: Walk the accountant who signs off on returns through every rule before it runs: which forms each checklist expects, who signs the engagement letter, and when an invoice is held. The app follows your rules and gives no tax advice.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Run the checklists for 10 clients from last season whose files you already have. Confirm that each upload is read as the right form and year, that reminders name the right item, and that partners hear only about late items.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Once document requests run cleanly, add the next job, such as W-9s or the status board. Each one is a new prompt on the same app and database, and the board can then show every return with its engagement letter and documents.

faq_plan.a: Tax automation is software that runs the repeated steps around tax work: requesting documents, reading forms, sending reminders, and moving each return to its next step. People still make every tax decision. In a firm, the paperwork moves on its own while preparers and reviewers keep the judgment calls.

faq_plan.q: How do I set up tax automation?
faq_plan.a: Start with one job, such as client document requests. Describe the checklist, the reminder day, and who hears about late items to Emergent's AI automation builder, and it builds the workflow, the client upload page, and the database. Test it on last season's clients, ask your accountant to check each rule, and then add the next job.

faq_plan.q: What do tax automation tools connect to?
faq_plan.a: An app Emergent builds can connect to your tax software, document storage, or accounting system, as long as the tool has an API. Client names and uploaded files move both ways, and a preparer never retypes them. Before you plan the first job, list which of your current tools offer an API.

faq_plan.q: Can tax automation read scanned tax documents?
faq_plan.a: Yes. An AI step reads each scanned tax form and pulls out the details your checklist needs, like the form name and year, then files it under the right client. A preparer confirms any value the AI marks as uncertain before the item counts as received.

faq_plan.q: Can tax automation collect W-9 forms from contractors?
faq_plan.a: Yes. The app can send a W-9 request with an upload link as soon as a contractor is added, and hold their invoices until the form is in. The IRS says to use Form W-9 to provide your correct Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) to the person who is required to file an information return with the IRS. Have your accountant review how you store the forms.

faq_plan.q: Does tax automation file returns or give tax advice?
faq_plan.a: No. The app requests documents, sends reminders, and tracks each return's status. Your preparers prepare and file returns in their own tax software. Payment records can be kept ready for Form 1099-NEC, which the IRS says to use to report nonemployee compensation. Tax decisions stay with your accountant.

faq_plan.q: How does tax automation track unsigned engagement letters?
faq_plan.a: It gives every letter a status, sent, signed, or overdue, and you pick the number of days before an overdue letter goes to a partner. Keep the signed copy on the client record. Next season's letter can then start from it, with only the fee and the year changed.

faq_plan.q: Where does tax automation store client data?
faq_plan.a: In an app Emergent builds, client records sit in a database you own. Emergent has SOC 2 Type I and ISO 27001. On paid plans the full code can go to your GitHub, where your IT lead can check who opens client records. Keep Social Security numbers out of reminders and send a link to the record instead.

faq_plan.q: Is there a task limit on tax automation during busy season?
faq_plan.a: No, not in an app Emergent builds, which has no task cap. The week before a deadline runs the same as a quiet week in July. If you compare platforms, check what each one does when a monthly limit is reached before you rely on it in March.

faq_plan.q: What documents should tax automation request from each client?
faq_plan.a: Request the forms on the client's prior-year return, such as W-2s, 1099s, and a Form 1098. Then add a short question about anything new this year, like a new job, a home sale, or a new dependent. Have your accountant review the list before it goes out.

plan.angle: The top 10 are enterprise tax software vendors (Thomson Reuters, RSM, Avalara), a few tax-prep AI products, a Reddit thread and a webinar, all selling a product or talking about the future of the profession. None shows the paperwork around a return moving on its own. This page shows four jobs a tax practice or a small business runs every season, each with its trigger, its rule and its record: a document checklist built from last year's return, W-9s collected before a contractor's first payment, engagement letters signed before prep starts, and a board of returns by status against the firm's own cutoff. The app organizes the work and the records; it gives no tax advice, calculates no tax and files nothing.
